texts: Commercial claims are more complex: more code requirements, more stakeholders, more ways for carriers to undervalue the loss. Michael's development background means nothing gets missed.
You always have final say on any settlement
When a business burns, payroll, customers, suppliers and the landlord all wait on the same scope. We write that scope first.
Loss of income and extra expense, built from your books by a forensic accountant.
Tenant improvements vs. building: who owns what, and whose policy pays.
Inventory and equipment, at replacement cost where the policy allows.
Code: we meet building officials early, so the rebuild scope reflects what the city will actually require.
Xactimate and IH reports: we rebuild the carrier's estimate line by line, and read the industrial hygienist's report before the carrier does.
Business interruption and loss of income
Ordinance or law and seismic code upgrades
Call Before the Carrier Sets the Narrative.
Your insurance company has an adjuster protecting their interests. You have the right to one too.
Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM Pacific
